WORKPLACE SMOKING PROHIBITION — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

PURPOSE
Acme, Inc. maintains this California Workplace Smoking Prohibition Information Sheet to describe the general prohibition on smoking of tobacco products in enclosed places of employment under California Labor Code section 6404.5, the statute's own defined terms, its listed exceptions, and its enforcement mechanism, for the information of employees including Jordan Lee. This information sheet states facts about California law; it does not determine whether any particular space, area, or situation at Acme, Inc. is or is not covered by section 6404.5, and it is not a statement that Acme, Inc.'s current smoking policy does or does not comply with the statute.

THE GENERAL PROHIBITION
California Labor Code section 6404.5, subdivision (c) provides that "[a]n employer or owner-operator of an owner-operated business shall not knowingly or intentionally permit, and a person shall not engage in, the smoking of tobacco products at a place of employment or in an enclosed space." The Legislature's stated intent in enacting the statute was "to prohibit the smoking of tobacco products in all (100 percent of) enclosed places of employment in this state, as covered by this section, thereby eliminating the need of local governments to enact workplace smoking restrictions within their respective jurisdictions."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "It is the intent of the Legislature in enacting this section to prohibit the smoking of tobacco products in all (100 percent of) enclosed places of employment in this state, as covered by this section, thereby eliminating the need of local governments to enact workplace smoking restrictions within their respective jurisdictions."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(a), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subd. (a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  "An employer or owner-operator of an owner-operated business shall not knowingly or intentionally permit, and a person shall not engage in, the smoking of tobacco products at a place of employment or in an enclosed space."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(c), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subd. (c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  Known gap: Both quotations come from Cal. Labor Code section 6404.5 -- the subdivision (a) legislative-intent quote and the subdivision (c) operative prohibition quote are two subdivisions of the same statutory section and are not independent of one another. The statutory text was fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two separate curl requests with different User-Agent strings, both returning HTTP 200 with byte-identical (whitespace-normalized) content; each quoted passage was confirmed programmatically as an exact, whitespace-normalized substring of that fetched text. This clause states the general rule; it does not state what counts as an "enclosed space" or a "place of employment" (addressed in the following clauses), nor whether any specific location is covered.

"ENCLOSED SPACE" AND "OWNER-OPERATED BUSINESS" DEFINED
Labor Code section 6404.5, subdivision (b) provides that "'[e]nclosed space' includes covered parking lots, lobbies, lounges, waiting areas, elevators, stairwells, and restrooms that are a structural part of the building and not specifically defined in subdivision (e)." The same subdivision defines an "owner-operated business" as "a business having no employees, independent contractors, or volunteers, in which the owner-operator of the business is the only worker."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "“Enclosed space” includes covered parking lots, lobbies, lounges, waiting areas, elevators, stairwells, and restrooms that are a structural part of the building and not specifically defined in subdivision (e)."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(b), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subd. (b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  "an “owner-operated business” shall mean a business having no employees, independent contractors, or volunteers, in which the owner-operator of the business is the only worker."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(b), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subd. (b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  Known gap: Both defined terms are quoted from the same subdivision, section 6404.5(b), and are not independent of one another as sources, though they define two distinct terms used elsewhere in the statute. The statutory text was fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two separate curl requests with different User-Agent strings, both returning HTTP 200 with byte-identical (whitespace-normalized) content; the quoted passages were confirmed programmatically as exact, whitespace-normalized substrings of that fetched text. The statute's definition of "enclosed space" is an inclusive, non-exhaustive list (it uses "includes") rather than a closed, exhaustive definition, and it expressly excludes areas "specifically defined in subdivision (e)" -- the statute's list of places that do not count as a "place of employment" at all, covered in a separate clause below. This clause does not state whether any particular room, area, or structure at any specific workplace meets this definition.

STATUTORY EXCEPTIONS -- WHAT IS NOT A "PLACE OF EMPLOYMENT"
Labor Code section 6404.5, subdivision (e) provides that "[f]or purposes of this section, 'place of employment' does not include any of the following:" (1) "Retail or wholesale tobacco shops and private smokers' lounges"; (2) "Cabs of motortrucks, as defined in Section 410 of the Vehicle Code, or truck tractors, as defined in Section 655 of the Vehicle Code, if nonsmoking employees are not present"; (3) "Theatrical production sites, if smoking is an integral part of the story in the theatrical production"; (4) "Medical research or treatment sites, if smoking is integral to the research and treatment being conducted"; (5) "Private residences, except for private residences licensed as family day care homes where smoking is prohibited pursuant to Section 1596.795 of the Health and Safety Code"; and (6) "Patient smoking areas in long-term health care facilities, as defined in Section 1418 of the Health and Safety Code."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "For purposes of this section, “place of employment” does not include any of the following:"
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(e), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subd. (e)(1)-(6) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  "Cabs of motortrucks, as defined in Section 410 of the Vehicle Code, or truck tractors, as defined in Section 655 of the Vehicle Code, if nonsmoking employees are not present."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(e)(2), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subd. (e)(2) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  "Private residences, except for private residences licensed as family day care homes where smoking is prohibited pursuant to Section 1596.795 of the Health and Safety Code."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(e)(5), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subd. (e)(5) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  Known gap: All six quoted items are paragraphs of the same subdivision, section 6404.5(e), and are not independent of one another as sources, though each defines a separately numbered, distinct exclusion. The statutory text was fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two separate curl requests with different User-Agent strings, both returning HTTP 200 with byte-identical (whitespace-normalized) content; each quoted item was confirmed programmatically as an exact, whitespace-normalized substring of that fetched text. This is the CURRENT list under the statute as last amended (Stats. 2023, Ch. 182, Sec. 3, effective January 1, 2024, per the statute's own end-of-section history note); it does not include exemptions that may have existed under earlier, superseded versions of this section, and this clause does not attempt to summarize the statute's amendment history beyond noting the current effective date. This clause states what the statute itself excludes from the definition of "place of employment"; it does not state whether any specific business, room, or vehicle at any specific workplace falls within one of these exclusions -- for example, none of the retail-tobacco-shop, private-residence, hotel, or small-business exclusions found in earlier versions of this law necessarily still exist in the current text quoted above, and this clause does not represent that any exclusion beyond the six quoted here currently exists.

EMPLOYER STEPS REGARDING NONEMPLOYEE SMOKERS
Labor Code section 6404.5, subdivision (d) provides that an employer or owner-operator "who permits any nonemployee access to their place of employment or owner-operated business on a regular basis has not acted knowingly or intentionally in violation of this section if the employer or owner-operator has taken the following reasonable steps to prevent smoking by a nonemployee": posting signs -- where smoking is prohibited throughout the building, "a sign stating 'No smoking' shall be posted at each entrance," and where smoking is permitted in designated areas, "a sign stating 'Smoking is prohibited except in designated areas' shall be posted at each entrance" -- and having "requested, when appropriate, that a nonemployee who is smoking refrain from smoking in the enclosed workplace or owner-operated business."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "an employer or owner-operator of an owner-operated business who permits any nonemployee access to their place of employment or owner-operated business on a regular basis has not acted knowingly or intentionally in violation of this section if the employer or owner-operator has taken the following reasonable steps to prevent smoking by a nonemployee:"
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(d), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subd. (d) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  "Posted clear and prominent signs, as follows: (A) Where smoking is prohibited throughout the building or structure, a sign stating “No smoking” shall be posted at each entrance to the building or structure. (B) Where smoking is permitted in designated areas of the building or structure, a sign stating “Smoking is prohibited except in designated areas” shall be posted at each entrance to the building or structure."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(d)(1), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subd. (d)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  "Has requested, when appropriate, that a nonemployee who is smoking refrain from smoking in the enclosed workplace or owner-operated business."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(d)(2), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subd. (d)(2) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  Known gap: All quoted language comes from the same subdivision, section 6404.5(d), and is not independent of one another as a source. The statutory text was fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two separate curl requests with different User-Agent strings, both returning HTTP 200 with byte-identical (whitespace-normalized) content; the quoted passages were confirmed programmatically as exact, whitespace-normalized substrings of that fetched text. Subdivision (d) describes what the statute treats as "reasonable steps" for purposes of a safe harbor against a knowing-or-intentional violation involving a nonemployee's smoking -- it does not itself impose a freestanding, independent posting requirement outside that context, and this clause does not state that any specific set of signage or requests does or does not satisfy the statute for any particular workplace. The subdivision also states that "reasonable steps" does not include physically ejecting a nonemployee or requiring a request under circumstances risking physical harm to the employer, an employee, or the owner-operator; this clause summarizes but does not separately quote that limiting language.

PENALTY AND ENFORCEMENT
Labor Code section 6404.5, subdivision (i) provides that "[a] violation of the prohibition set forth in subdivision (c) is an infraction, punishable by a fine not to exceed one hundred dollars ($100) for a first violation, two hundred dollars ($200) for a second violation within one year, and five hundred dollars ($500) for a third and for each subsequent violation within one year," and that this "subdivision shall be enforced by local law enforcement agencies, including, but not limited to, local health departments, as determined by the local governing body." Subdivision (j) separately provides that, "[n]otwithstanding Section 6309, the division is not required to respond to any complaint regarding the smoking of tobacco products in an enclosed space at a place of employment, unless the employer has been found guilty pursuant to subdivision (i) of a third violation of subdivision (c) within the previous year."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "A violation of the prohibition set forth in subdivision (c) is an infraction, punishable by a fine not to exceed one hundred dollars ($100) for a first violation, two hundred dollars ($200) for a second violation within one year, and five hundred dollars ($500) for a third and for each subsequent violation within one year. This subdivision shall be enforced by local law enforcement agencies, including, but not limited to, local health departments, as determined by the local governing body."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(i), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subd. (i) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  "Notwithstanding Section 6309, the division is not required to respond to any complaint regarding the smoking of tobacco products in an enclosed space at a place of employment, unless the employer has been found guilty pursuant to subdivision (i) of a third violation of subdivision (c) within the previous year."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(j), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subd. (j) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  Known gap: Both quoted subdivisions, (i) and (j), come from the same statutory section, section 6404.5, and are not independent of one another as sources, though they address two distinct points: the penalty amount and enforcing body, and a separate limit on the Division of Occupational Safety and Health's ("the division"'s) own duty to respond to complaints. The statutory text was fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two separate curl requests with different User-Agent strings, both returning HTTP 200 with byte-identical (whitespace-normalized) content; the quoted passages were confirmed programmatically as exact, whitespace-normalized substrings of that fetched text. This clause does not independently verify the cross-referenced Labor Code section 6309 (defining "the division"'s general complaint-response duty) -- that section was not separately fetched this session -- and states only what section 6404.5 itself says about the exception to it. This clause does not state that any particular local agency will or will not act on any specific report.

ELECTRONIC SMOKING DEVICES AND VAPING
Labor Code section 6404.5 does not define "smoking" or "tobacco product" on its own terms; instead, subdivision (l) provides that, "[f]or purposes of this section, 'smoking' has the same meaning as in subdivision (c) of Section 22950.5 of the Business and Professions Code," and subdivision (m) provides that "'tobacco product' means a product or device as defined in subdivision (d) of Section 22950.5" of that code. Business and Professions Code section 22950.5, subdivision (c) defines "smoking" to mean "inhaling, exhaling, burning, or carrying any lighted or heated cigar, cigarette, or pipe, or any other lighted or heated tobacco or plant product intended for inhalation, whether natural or synthetic, in any manner or in any form," and further provides that "'[s]moking' includes the use of an electronic smoking device that creates an aerosol or vapor, in any manner or in any form, or the use of any oral smoking device for the purpose of circumventing the prohibition of smoking." Subdivision (d) of that same section defines "tobacco product" to include "[a]n electronic device that delivers nicotine or other vaporized liquids to the person inhaling from the device, including, but not limited to, an electronic cigarette, cigar, pipe, or hookah."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "For purposes of this section, “smoking” has the same meaning as in subdivision (c) of Section 22950.5 of the Business and Professions Code."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 6404.5(l), (m), Cal. Lab. Code § 6404.5, subds. (l), (m) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6404.5.)
  "“Smoking” includes the use of an electronic smoking device that creates an aerosol or vapor, in any manner or in any form, or the use of any oral smoking device for the purpose of circumventing the prohibition of smoking."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 22950.5(c), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 22950.5, subd. (c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=22950.5.)
  "An electronic device that delivers nicotine or other vaporized liquids to the person inhaling from the device, including, but not limited to, an electronic cigarette, cigar, pipe, or hookah."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 22950.5(d), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 22950.5, subd. (d)(1)(B) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=22950.5.)
  Known gap: This clause draws on two genuinely distinct, independently numbered code sections: Labor Code section 6404.5 (subdivisions (l) and (m), which are two subdivisions of the same section and not independent of each other) and Business and Professions Code section 22950.5 (subdivisions (c) and (d), likewise two subdivisions of the same section and not independent of each other). The Labor Code and Business and Professions Code sections are independent of one another as sources. All statutory text was fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two separate curl requests with different User-Agent strings for each code section, all four returning HTTP 200 with byte-identical (whitespace-normalized) content; every quoted passage was confirmed programmatically as an exact, whitespace-normalized substring of the fetched text. Business and Professions Code section 22950.5 is itself part of a different statutory scheme (the Stop Tobacco Access to Kids Enforcement Act) that Labor Code section 6404.5 incorporates only by cross-reference for the meaning of these two specific terms; this clause does not address any other part of that Act. The section 22950.5 text fetched carries its own amendment history note (Stats. 2016, 2nd Ex. Sess., Ch. 7, Sec. 1, effective June 9, 2016), consistent with California's 2016 expansion of its smoking laws to cover electronic cigarettes.
